title: [Chapitre] VI. Analysis situs (deuxième mouture) : notes manuscrites (18-20/06/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: in the 1986 'Analysis situs (deuxième mouture)' notes Grothendieck sets up an axiomatic tame-topology framework. There is a set 𝓕 of 'figures' F, each with a combinatorial poset F̃ of cells and a set comb(F) of combinatorial sub-figures, plus a distinguished class M of basic figures ('cells' X with boundary ∂X). There are three relations: G ≤ F (sub-figure), F' ≪ F (F' is a refinement carried by F), and x ∥ F' (x is compatible with, i.e. a union of pieces of, F'). On p.85 'subdivision' is defined: F' ≼ F means F' ≪ F and every x ∈ comb F satisfies x ∥ F'. Page 85 shows that ≼ is an order relation and that it is stable under restriction to a sub-figure G ≤ F.

This page does three things.

(1) It finishes the proof of the Corollary. Suppose F = Sup F_i and F'_i = F'|F_i. Then F' ≼ F iff F'_i ≼ F_i for all i. Necessity follows from the restriction proposition. For sufficiency, take x ∈ comb F. Since comb F = ∪ comb F_i, x lies in some comb F_{i0}. Since F'_{i0} ≼ F_{i0}, we get x ∥ F'_{i0}, and the lemma of p.82 turns this into x ∥ F'. So subdivision is a local property for coverings by sub-figures.

(2) It titles 'Corollaire 2: recollement des subdivisions': compatible subdivisions of the pieces F_i should glue to a subdivision of F. Only the title is written.

(3) It states 'Ax 14', marked 'facultatif' in the margin, as an axiom rather than a theorem. If G ≤ F and G' ≼ G is a subdivision, there exists a subdivision F' ≼ F inducing G' on G. This is the analogue of the classical PL fact that a subdivision of a subcomplex extends to the whole complex. Grothendieck sketches a reduction: by gluing, plus transfinite induction (ordinary induction if F̃ is finite), reduce to the case where F = X is a single cell in M.

A closing Remark asks for a canonical choice: the least fine (maximal for ≼) extension, as in the set-theoretic case. This leads on p.87 to Ax (fac) 14 bis, where the extension leaves cells outside G unchanged (F̃'∖G̃' ≅ F̃∖G̃ with an explicit order). It also leads to 14 ter: a subdivision of ∂X extends uniquely to a subdivision X' of the cell X with the same interior cell, as in regular cell / polyhedral complexes.
errors: Sufficiency proof: the transcription's 'prouvons qu'on peut avoir x ∥ F'' should read 'prouvons qu'on a x ∥ F''. The hypothesis used should be F'_{i0} ≼ F_{i0} (subdivision), not ≤; the image shows the subdivision symbol with index i.
The lemma of p.82 is invoked for F'_{i0} = F'|F_{i0}; the step is valid only if that lemma gives x ∥ F'|G ⇒ x ∥ F' for x ∈ comb G, which it does per p.85.
Corollary 2 (gluing) is only titled. The existence of a glued F' from compatible F'_i is not proved and presumably needs a separate sheaf-type axiom on 𝓕.

Ax 14 is not proved, only reduced in outline. The transfinite induction needs a well-ordering of cells compatible with the face order, and a gluing statement at limit stages. This is presumably why it is demoted to an optional axiom.

ideas.what: Locality of subdivision: F' is a subdivision of F iff its restrictions to a covering family of sub-figures are subdivisions
ideas.modern_name: local character of subdivision / sheaf property of refinements
ideas.usually_credited_to: folklore in PL topology (Whitehead, Zeeman, Hudson)

ideas.what: Extension of a subdivision of a closed sub-figure to the whole figure (Ax 14, 'facultatif')
ideas.modern_name: extension of subdivisions of subcomplexes (PL topology); refinement extension in o-minimal cell decompositions
ideas.usually_credited_to: classical PL topology (Whitehead 1939, Zeeman, Rourke–Sanderson); o-minimal analogue van den Dries

ideas.what: Request for a canonical, coarsest extension, modifying only cells meeting G (leads to 14 bis/ter: unique cell structure on X given a subdivision of ∂X)
ideas.modern_name: minimal extension of a boundary subdivision; regular CW / polyhedral complexes where a cell keeps its interior
ideas.usually_credited_to: standard for regular cell complexes (Björner face-poset theory, Lundell–Weingram)
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme §5-6 only programmatically discusses 'topologie modérée'

missed.claim: The axiomatic treatment of subdivisions inside an abstract 'figures/cells' framework (an axiom system for tame topology) is unpublished, and the extension axiom is left optional with only a reduction sketch. Today's comparable frameworks (o-minimality, regular cell posets) do not state it in this form.
missed.quote: Ax 14 Soient G ≤ F, G' ≼ G. Alors ∃ subdivision F' de F qui induise G'
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Marginal. It documents which properties Grothendieck considered optional axioms rather than theorems in his tame-topology programme, but the mathematical content is classical.

deep.surprise_reason: Routine PL-topology-style facts (locality and gluing of subdivisions, extension from a subcomplex) recast in Grothendieck's unpublished axiomatic 'analysis situs'. Interesting only as documentation of the programme, not as a new result.
transcription_corrections: 'At 14' should be 'Ax 14' (axiom, consistent with 'Ax (fac) 14 bis' on p.87), not 'Th 14'.
The diagonal margin note reads 'facultatif', not 'Je recolle bien'.
'prouvons qu'on peut avoir x ∥ F'' should be 'prouvons qu'on a x ∥ F''.
'comme F_i' ≤ F_i' is 'comme F'_i ≼ F_i' (subdivision symbol).
In the Remark, the struck word is unclear; read '...la moins fine (maximale) parmi celles qui ont la propriété voulue'.
